newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money digs in around 3 pct despite drain.
newsitem.headline: German call money digs in around 3 pct despite drain.

text.p: German call money rates continued to trade mostly steady around three percent, unmoved by news the Bundesbank had drained funds from the market at its weekly auction.
"Rates are still trending around the three percent level, the market still has enough liquidity," said one dealer.

Although the Bundesbank on Wednesday drained 1.9 billion marks from the system at its weekly tender, dealers said the market still sufficient funds, particularly since many banks had expected a slightly bigger drain.

Monthly reserve holdings, standing at 44.3 billion marks on Tuesday, down only slightly from Monday's 44.6 billion mark level, also indicated that call money rates should continue to trade around the same levels.
Monthly holdings stood at 43.9 billion marks on Tuesday, which was up from 43.7 billion marks held on Monday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was set at 3.03800 percent on Wednesday, after 3.03733 percent.
